title: Amar Singh’s Confidence Hardens Into Overconfidence

blocks.text: The review of forces continues and swells Amar Singh's pride. After he has inspected the infantry soldiers, the sight of artillery, musketeers, and massed troops persuades him that the encounter is already decided in his favor.

Reports estimate Baghel Singh's contingent at a smaller number, and Amar Singh immediately converts that intelligence into swagger. He talks as though it will be easy to capture S. Baghel Singh, insisting that even a wider Khalsa response would not be able to rescue him once the campaign closes in.

The page thus turns military preparation into a study of misjudgment. What should have been reconnaissance becomes the fuel for a boastful certainty that underestimates both Baghel Singh and the fighting reputation of the Singhs.
